Since c_2025_8_D433 is already matched with the other redemption disclosures, and no other 2025 record covers Series W specifically, this 2024 record has no unique counterpart for its specific dividend/reset topic.

comparisons.peer_topic: 2025 Issuance of Series Z Preferred Stock
comparisons.peer_summary: In January 2025, the firm issued 76,000 shares of Series Z 6.85% Fixed-Rate Reset Non-Cumulative Preferred Stock, which has a $25,000 liquidation preference, is redeemable at the firm's option starting February 10, 2030, and pays semi-annual dividends at 6.85% per annum until that date, thereafter resetting to 2.461% plus the five-year treasury rate.
comparisons.comparison: Both Citi and Goldman Sachs disclose the specific dividend reset mechanics for a fixed-rate reset preferred stock series. Citi's Series W resets to the five-year treasury rate plus 3.597% after December 10, 2025, while Goldman's Series Z resets to the five-year treasury rate plus 2.461% after February 10, 2030. Both structures utilize a fixed period followed by a floating rate tied to treasury yields.

sentences.text: Dividends are payable quarterly on March 10, June 10, September 10 and December 10 at a fixed rate until, but excluding, December 10, 2025, thereafter payable quarterly on the same dates at a fixed rate that resets on the Series W reset date and every five years thereafter equal to the five-year treasury rate plus 3.597%, in each case when, as and if declared by the Citi Board of Directors.

Dividends on Series Z Preferred Stock, if declared, are payable semi-annually at (i) 6.85% per annum from the issuance date to, but excluding, February 10, 2030 and, thereafter, (ii) 2.461% per annum plus the five-year treasury rate.

peer_results.rationale: JPMorgan's candidates focus on the general dividend policy reference rates (jpm_2024_8_D500) and the issuance of Series NN (jpm_2024_8_D504). comparisons.peer_summary: Series M preferred stock dividends are payable semiannually until September 15, 2026, and quarterly thereafter.
comparisons.comparison: Citi and Morgan Stanley both disclose a transition in dividend payment frequency for their preferred stock series. Citi's Series W pays quarterly dividends, while Morgan Stanley's Series M pays semiannually until a specific date (September 15, 2026) before transitioning to quarterly payments. Both disclosures highlight the specific schedule change tied to a future date.
